title: Rotational Work, Kinetic Energy, and the Rotational Work-Energy Theorem
learning_objective: Apply work-energy principles to rotating rigid bodies, relating applied torque to angular displacement and changes in rotational kinetic energy.
explanation: When an external torque $\tau$ acts on a rigid body rotating about a fixed axis, the work done during an infinitesimal angular displacement $d\theta$ is: $$dW = \tau \, d\theta$$ Integrating over finite angular displacement yields the net rotational work: $$W_{\text{net}} = \int_{\theta_1}^{\theta_2} \tau_{\text{net}}(\theta) \, d\theta$$ Applying Newton's rotational dynamic relation $\tau_{\text{net}} = I \alpha = I \frac{d\omega}{dt} = I \omega \frac{d\omega}{d\theta}$, the work integral transforms into: $$W_{\text{net}} = \int_{\omega_i}^{\omega_f} I \omega \, d\omega = \frac{1}{2} I \omega_f^2 - \frac{1}{2} I \omega_i^2 = \Delta K_{\text{rot}}$$ This constitutes the Rotational Work-Energy Theorem. The instantaneous rotational power delivered by a torque is: $$P = \frac{dW}{dt} = \tau \omega$$ In a conservative system, the total mechanical energy $E = K_{\text{trans}} + K_{\text{rot}} + U$ remains strictly conserved.
intuition: Rotational kinetic energy is the rotational analogue of translational $\frac{1}{2} m v^2$, replacing mass $m$ with moment of inertia $I$ and linear speed $v$ with angular velocity $\omega$. Just as a linear force pushing an object over distance $dx$ does work $F dx$, a twisting torque turning an object through angle $d\theta$ does rotational work $\tau d\theta$.
formal_definition: The kinetic energy associated with pure rotation of a rigid body about a fixed axis with angular velocity $\omega$: $$K_{\text{rot}} = \frac{1}{2} I \omega^2$$ and the net work done by torques on the body equals its change in rotational kinetic energy: $W_{\text{net}} = \Delta K_{\text{rot}}$.
assumptions: Fixed axis of rotation in an inertial frame
Rigid body condition ensuring identical angular velocity omega for all parts
Negligible internal dissipative shear within the rigid body
boundary_conditions: Holds for fixed-axis rotation and for rotation about center of mass in accelerating bodies
For combined translation and rotation, total kinetic energy is K_total = 1/2 M v_cm^2 + 1/2 I_cm omega^2
source_references: Halliday, Resnick & Walker, Chapter 10, Section 10.8 (Work and Rotational Kinetic Energy)
University Physics, Chapter 9, Section 9.4 (Energy in Rotational Motion)
